name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.319.0 — fanout-driver: a red main gate now outranks DISPATCH, so the next planned lane is never dispatched onto a red main after --mark merged (a pending question still relays first); --mark gate-repaired re-loads the state after the long gate run and applies only its outcome, so a --mark returned that landed meanwhile is no longer clobbered; merging a fix lane with a queueId ticks its queue item through spec-queue done (whatever the gate colour, since the work is on main), warning instead of dying when the tick fails; and a green gate-repaired drops that lane's 'main gate red' line from the queued list, so the report no longer lists a repair that no longer exists. 7.318.0 — fix(review): finishMerge keeps the review state where the merge-strategy mark finds it until merge-back.sh cleanup exits 0, and cleanup lifts the agent harness's own 'claude agent' worktree lock — a failed close cleanup is re-runnable. 7.317.0 — spec-status no longer lets a queued prompt or decide item at the queue head seat itself as the only lane: queue prompt entries are excluded from top-pick and lane admission, so independent hardened specs fan out as parallel lanes while the prompt row still prints first in the Next block; --next order is unchanged. spec-queue's move/done/show/next/list/groom now refuse any unknown --flag (including --root) with exit 2 instead of silently acting on the cwd repo's queue.
